title: Auth sidecar proxy patterns for SDKs: rotation, streaming re-auth, and secret hygiene
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: Provide a robust, cross-language pattern for handling API keys, key rotation, enterprise SSO tokens, and secret hygiene in Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Deliver a primary in-SDK token auto-refresh + opaque token cache approach and an optional lightweight sidecar/auth-proxy for customers that cannot store long-lived secrets in process (air-gapped or high-compliance setups). Include ergonomics for streaming APIs so long-lived streams do not drop when a token rotates, and clear retry semantics when re-authentication is required.
background: Multiple enterprise customers have indicated the need to rotate API keys frequently, use SSO-issued ephemeral tokens, or run SDKs in environments that disallow process-local long-lived secrets. Current SDKs accept static API keys and provide minimal guidance for rotation + streaming re-auth. This ticket enumerates patterns, trade-offs, and an implementation plan across Python/TS/Go SDKs plus an optional Go sidecar binary for constrained environments.
decision_record: Adopt a hybrid pattern: 1) Default: in-SDK Authenticator interface that performs non-blocking background refresh of tokens with jittered backoff; 2) Optional: sidecar auth-proxy that issues local short-lived session tokens to SDKs via Unix socket/localhost and handles secret storage/rotation on behalf of the app. The in-SDK path is the recommended developer experience; the sidecar is for enterprise compliance or legacy app constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a common Authenticator interface and default to environment/API-key usage with auto-refresh when ephemeral tokens are configured
Streaming client libraries can silently renew credentials mid-stream without failing in >95% of simulated key-rotation events
Sidecar binary (Go) prototype can be launched in local dev and deployed in Dedicated/Private customers; SDKs can automatically detect and use it over Unix socket or HTTP localhost
Integration tests covering 401-on-send, 401-during-stream, and 5xx-with-retry are added to CI for each SDK
Documentation (README + migration guide) published and linked from SDK quickstart
Security review completed and threat model added to the repo
implementation_steps: Design common Authenticator interface and token lifecycle spec (TTL, refresh_window, retry_policy)
Implement background refresh + lock-free token swap for Python/TS/Go SDKs
Add streaming token rebind handling: keep-alive + on-401 handshake to re-auth and resume stream where supported
Build a minimal Go sidecar auth-proxy prototype that supports: static API keys, KMS/HSM integration, OIDC device code flow, and token aliasing for zero-downtime rotation
Create integration test harness that injects rotation events and validates client recovery
Add telemetry hooks: auth.status, auth.refresh.count, auth.refresh.latency, auth.failure_reason
Docs + migration guide + examples for each language
Security review and threat model updates
Rollout: alpha SDK version (opt-in) -> beta with sidecar enabled for a pilot customer -> GA
design_tradeoffs_and_notes: In-SDK refresh is simplest for most users and reduces operational overhead, but some enterprise customers require secrets to be isolated from application process memory. A sidecar adds operational complexity but centralizes key management and auditing. Trade-offs: sidecar increases network hops and introduces a single point for local failure (mitigated by simple fallback to in-SDK 'short-lived direct' mode). Streaming re-auth mid-stream requires protocol support from the server: we will add a 1001 reauth frame on the wire and a short handshake to resume. If servers cannot support resumption, SDKs will attempt best-effort to re-open stream and replay idempotent context where possible.
engineering_notes: Implement token caching using lock-free atomic pointer swap or double-checked locking depending on language. Python: prefer threading.Timer or background asyncio.Task depending on sync/async client. TS: use fetch + AbortController to cancel and refresh in-flight requests if necessary; provide both browser and node implementations. Go: use context-aware background goroutine with context cancellation. For sidecar comms, prefer Unix domain socket for on-prem for security; fallback to localhost HTTP if socket unavailable.
security_considerations: - Store only short-lived tokens in-process. - Encourage OS keyring usage for persisting refresh tokens (Keyring library for Python, keytar for Node, os/user credential stores for Go). - Sidecar must support KMS/HSM-backed key storage and rotation logs for audit. - All sidecar <-> SDK comms must be authenticated and use local ACL file or ephemeral TLS with loopback certificates generated at startup. - Must avoid logging secrets; redact in all telemetry.
test_plan: Unit tests for Authenticator in each SDK, e2e integration tests that: (1) rotate server-side API key and validate client refresh within SLAs; (2) simulate SSO token expiry mid-stream and verify graceful reconnection; (3) measure added tail latency introduced by refresh; (4) sidecar failure modes (crash, high latency) and SDK fallbacks. Run integration harness in CI against a local mock auth server and periodically against staging infra.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flags behind opt-in env var SDK_AUTH_SIDE_CAR=1 for sidecar behavior and SDK_AUTH_AUTorefresh=1 for in-SDK path. 2) Release alpha SDKs and request two pilot customers (one Dedicated, one Private) to validate sidecar operations. 3) Iterate from feedback, complete security review, and ship GA in sdk-2025.03 with migration docs. 4) Monitor auth.refresh.failure_rate and customer support tickets for unexpected regressions.
open_questions: Should the SDK expose hooks for custom keyrings or only provide built-in integrations?
What is the exact protocol for stream resumption: server-driven frame vs client-initiated reconnect + resume token?
Do we require the sidecar to rotate API keys automatically using a configured rotation window, or only expose rotate-on-request?

customer_cases: Financial data provider needs key rotation every 24 hours and cannot have long-lived keys in process memory
Healthcare customer requires audit logs and HSM storage for signing API keys used to mint session tokens
SaaS startup wants zero-downtime rolling rotation of API keys while keeping streaming sessions alive for customers
risks: Sidecar adoption could fragment support surface and increase operational load for platform. Streaming reauth may not be possible in all server contexts; fallback reconnects could cause duplicate in-flight requests for non-idempotent operations. Telemetry gaps could obscure rotation failures—ensure metrics and alerts are in place.
next_steps: Finish Python fix for lock contention, finalize sidecar security model (local TLS + ACL), coordinate pilot with two customers, and schedule security review by 2025-03-20. Assign documentation owner to publish migration guide.
